title: "Free card upgrade" needing CVV and expiry vs. upgrade offer accepted in the app
summary: A caller from Kaveri Bank offers the recipient a free upgrade of their credit card to a higher tier with a bigger limit. In the fraud case, the caller says the upgrade must be "verified" on the call and asks for the card's expiry date and CVV. In the legitimate case, the caller describes the same offer and tells the recipient to accept it in the Cards section of the Kaveri Bank app if interested. The new card will be posted to the registered address and no card details are needed.

shared_setting.pretext: an upgrade to a premium card with a higher limit of [AMOUNT_1] (₹1,00,000–₹5,00,000) and a first-year annual fee waiver.
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult Kaveri Bank credit-card holder; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers say the offer is "pre-approved" and "limited period".

fraud.label_rationale: The caller asks for the card's CVV and expiry date on the call. Together with the card number, these allow card-not-present payments; banks never ask customers for them.
fraud.caller_objective: Obtain the card's expiry date and CVV, and later any OTP, to make purchases.
stable_facts: The caller already quotes the card's last four digits and the recipient's name.
The caller says the upgrade is "activated only after verification" on this call.
The caller says the old card will be blocked if the upgrade is not verified today.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may repeat the request, mention the OTP that "will come next", or give up. Asking for an OTP after CVV is part of the same card-credential mechanism and is allowed. The caller must not switch to a link, app install, or payment. The legitimate caller must not ask for any card detail, code, or payment after the branch.

must_preserve: card last-four, new limit, and fee waiver in both
app acceptance and explicit "no card details" (_L)
may_vary: up to 2 filler turns before turn 3
must_not_emit: real card-number or CVV formats beyond a placeholder

ambiguities: Pre-approved", "limited period", and "fee waiver" appear in both cases. The label depends on the CVV and expiry request.
The resistant condition is the same in both columns on purpose: declining an offer is neutral.
Mechanism overlap: bp_01 and bp_14 ask for an OTP; this card asks for CVV. They differ in the credential and in whether an SMS arrives during the call.

evidence_references.claim: Banks and genuine entities never ask for card details, CVV, or OTP (C01)
Impostors cite urgency or attractive offers to get CVV or OTP (C02)
Impostors share a few customer details to gain confidence (C03)
Fraud can be reported on 1930 / cybercrime.gov.in (C12)
